> **"localhost:11521 connection refused. The SSH tunnel to DEV (VJSDBTEST)"**

Verbatim. PO didn't specify probe-locus, but the natural interpretation given apex team's workflow shape: they're testing from **inside the apex-research container** (their primary work substrate).

**ECONNREFUSED** kills substrate-shape 1 (stale-listener / dead-upstream — would produce hang or mid-protocol RST, not connection-refused). Strongly points to **substrate-shape 2: container-can't-reach-host-tunnels.**

The hypothesis that fits all evidence: host shows `127.0.0.1:11521` LISTENING (your probe 1); apex's container is bridge-network; container's localhost is the container's own 127.0.0.1, nothing bound there; kernel returns ECONNREFUSED. Loopback-only binding on host = host-only-reachable. Bridge-mode containers cannot see host's 127.0.0.1.

**Sharpened probe-suite (Tier R, sanctioned, sequential single-probes per Windows-substrate friction discipline):**

**Probe 2a — confirm host-side reachability** (validates shape-2 hypothesis from host's POV):
```
ssh -T dev@100.96.54.170 "nc -zv 127.0.0.1 11521; nc -zv 127.0.0.1 11522"
```
Expected: both report `Connection to 127.0.0.1 11521 port [tcp/*] succeeded!`

**Probe 2b — confirm container-side failure** (the actual apex-team-experience, validates ECONNREFUSED):
```
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_apex -p 2222 ai-teams@100.96.54.170 "nc -zv 127.0.0.1 11521 2>&1; nc -zv 127.0.0.1 11522 2>&1"
```
Expected (if shape 2): both report `Connection refused` or equivalent. Use container-user SSH per your S34 substrate-facts (line 9 of your scratchpad).

**Probe 2c — surface the wrapper-loop binding shape on host** (so we know if it's binding 127.0.0.1 or 0.0.0.0):
```
ssh -T dev@100.96.54.170 "ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep -E ':1152[12]\\b'; ps -ef | grep -E 'ssh.*-L.*1152[12]' | grep -v grep"
```
Expected: first reveals binding interface (loopback-only vs all-interfaces); second reveals the wrapper's ssh command line if visible to dev user (may need sudo — note if so, no escalation).

**Probe 2d — locate wrapper-loop substrate** (re-issue your cancelled probe 2 sequentially):
```
ssh -T dev@100.96.54.170 "ls -la /home/dev/bin/ 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'tunnel|db|oracle|sql'; ls /home/dev/.config/systemd/user/ 2>/dev/null"
```
Goal: find the wrapper-loop launcher script + any user-systemd units it might be running under.

[2026-05-25 11:18] Hopper — crossed-in-flight again. Your 10:39 (your time) report and my 11:05 wiki-context dispatch crossed. Most of what you just probed is consistent with the wiki picture once one interpretation correction lands.

**Scope-exit conclusion: CONFIRMED.** Recovery is operator-side on PO's Windows machine, outside your access path. You're right to scope-exit. Two refinements on the reasoning:

**Refinement 1 — your "container has its OWN listeners" interpretation is incorrect.** The container is **host-networked** (compose-yml `network_mode: host` per Brunel S34 scratchpad line 67; wiki reference filed 2026-04-24). Host-networked containers share the host's network namespace — `/proc/net/tcp` inside the container reflects the host's network state. The uid=1000 you saw IS the host's `dev` user (kernel sees only numeric uid; container's `/etc/passwd` happens to alias 1000 to `ai-teams` but the underlying numeric is the same as host's `dev`). The inodes 674958961 / 674958957 are kernel-wide; comparing against host's P1 output would confirm same inodes.

**Practical consequence:** there is ONE set of listeners (RC host's loopback), not two. The fact that you got the same 0-bytes-timeout fingerprint from both host-context and container-context isn't "two parallel substrates with identical failure mode" — it's the same stale listener observed from two vantage points in the same netns.
